decisions.reason: As a technically adjacent extension of the firm's wafer portfolio, it likely remains above or near aspiration levels and is worth retaining given the growing semiconductor substrate market.
This product fits directly with the firm's established thin-wafer handling and carrier business, so management would likely see little reason to reallocate resources away from it.
Although newer and somewhat more uncertain, it builds on core glass-wafer capabilities and aligns with the firm's strategic move toward more complex packaging wafers.
The off-the-shelf brand is close to the core business and probably requires limited additional resources, making it easy to continue while it develops demand.

Because glass-based circuit boards are more distant from the firm's established offer, management would be more likely to drop them if results did not clearly meet aspirations and free resources for core substrate products.
